newsitem.title: RUSSIA: FORECAST- Russian c.bank sees slower M2 in 1997.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST- Russian c.bank sees slower M2 in 1997.

text.p: Russia's central bank forecasts growth in M2 money supply of 1.7-2.2 percent a month in 1997, compared with an estimated 2.5-2.9 percent this year, according to bank documents sent to parliament.
The documents show the bank forecast money supply growth of 22-30 percent for the whole of 1997. Monthly inflation will be 0.8-1.0 percent.
M2 rose an average 3.5 percent a month in the first half of this year. Prices have risen 17.3 percent so far this year.
The bank said it would increase money supply by 2.1-2.6 percent a month in the first half of next year and by 1.2-1.8 percent in the second.
The velocity of M2 -- the ratio of Gross Domestic Product to M2 -- would fall in 1996 to 9.0 from 10.4 in 1995 and 9.6 in 1994.

"Although the velocity of circulation of money is higher than in other countries with transition economies, an attempt artificially to lower it by an additional issue (of money) can only lead to growth in inflation," the bank said.
It said the natural way to lower the velocity would be to achieve economic growth.

The bank does not plan strict monthly targets for monetary supply. "The bank must be able to make flexible corrections to money supply within a half year and monthly monetary benchmarks will have an indicative function," the document said.
